page: Microsoft Azure L64s_v2 is a virtual machine instance from the LSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7551 processor operating at 3.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 16015 GB of Premium Storage capable capacity, while it does not contain any graphics processing units.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance falling into the bottom 10% and Geekbench single-core scores categorized in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core performance is more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all landing in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth for both small and large block reads and writes is average, and the instance demonstrates strong performance in the PassMark CPU encryption test, placing in the top 25%.

Given the high local storage capacity of 16015 GB and 512.0 GB of RAM, the L64s_v2 is designed for storage-intensive and database workloads that require high resource density. It is appropriate for database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks, which perform at average levels. However, it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks, text processing, or large-scale LLM text generation, where performance is poor. The hardware profile offers a balanced resource density for large datasets, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for high-capacity local storage needs without the overhead of GPU hardware.
description: Microsoft Azure L64s_v2 is an LSv2 family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7551 processor with 64 dedicated vCPUs, 32 physical cores, and a 3.2 GHz clock speed. It is configured with 512.0 GB of RAM and 16015 GB of Premium Storage capable local storage, with no GPU acceleration. Benchmark data shows a trade-off between weak single-core performance, which ranks in the bottom 10% to 25%, and average multi-core capabilities across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests. Notably, the instance achieves strong results in CPU encryption tests, placing in the top 25%. With its substantial local storage and memory capacity, the L64s_v2 is optimized for database operations, multi-threaded data processing, and static web serving, offering qualitative cost efficiency for storage-heavy workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute power.
